findings.title: Kaspersky Securelist: CyberStrikeAI in the wild - the use of AI in real-world attacks on organizations
findings.summary_md: Kaspersky's Cyber Threat Intelligence team identified a malicious campaign in which C2 agents controlled by an LLM-driven CyberStrikeAI framework targeted educational organizations across Africa and Latin America. The framework's implant is a conventional C2 beacon with no AI logic, while an LLM orchestrator on the control server plans actions, selects tools, and generates commands. Kaspersky published the analysis on November 2, 2026, roughly three hours before the story's first_seen timestamp, detailing reconnaissance, persistence, credential dumping, lateral movement, and data exfiltration completed within 3 to 4 days.

findings.title: Team Cymru: Tracking CyberStrikeAI - AI-Native Offensive Tools and MSS Ties
findings.summary_md: Team Cymru's telemetry research identified CyberStrikeAI service banners on attacker infrastructure and tracked 21 servers running the platform between January and February 2026. The post linked the framework to a campaign that compromised more than 600 FortiGate appliances across 55 countries. Published March 2, 2026, it provides the earliest public exploitation telemetry for CyberStrikeAI.

findings.title: BleepingComputer: CyberStrikeAI tool adopted by hackers for AI-powered attacks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported that Team Cymru's NetFlow analysis found a CyberStrikeAI banner on port 8080 of an attacker IP and network communications to FortiGate devices. The article described the framework as an open-source AI-powered offensive security tool used to breach Fortinet FortiGate devices worldwide. Published March 2, 2026 (March 3 UTC), it preceded the November 2 story by months.

findings.title: The Hacker News: Open-Source CyberStrikeAI Deployed in AI-Driven FortiGate Attacks Across 55 Countries
findings.summary_md: The Hacker News covered the campaign in which AI-powered CyberStrikeAI was linked to roughly 600 FortiGate breaches across 55 countries, with 21 IPs tied to China-based infrastructure. The report noted the tool's use for automated scanning and exploitation of internet-exposed FortiGate devices. Published March 3, 2026, it provided early news coverage of CyberStrikeAI's weaponization.

findings.title: Trend Micro: AI involvement in three attack infrastructures targeting Japan
findings.summary_md: Trend Micro researchers examined three exposed attacker infrastructures targeting Japanese organizations and confirmed abuse of CyberStrikeAI, an open-source AI-agent penetration-testing tool, in one of them. The report described 44 AI agents automating reconnaissance through data theft and noted a simplified-Chinese management console. Published October 23, 2026, it preceded the November 2 Kaspersky report.
